texts: mind won't sit still
I sat down to pray for five minutes and my thoughts ran off to the bills, the neighbour's remark, tomorrow's trip, and a song from childhood before I had said one word.
Write a doha about how the wandering mind runs after every passing thing, to the past, to the future, to every desire, and how it must be gently but firmly brought back and tamed.
Hither and thither it flits, this restless guest within, never at rest for even one breath; teach me to hold it.
my mind jumps around like crazy during meditation, got a doha for that?
From a single seed a hundred thoughts sprout, each running faster than the last; who can catch such a restless crop?
thoughts sprouting, seed
doha about a mind that keeps sprouting new thoughts, like a seed that never stops
Compose a verse about the mind that plants a seed of desire and instantly chases another, never staying with one thing, never finishing what it begins, and always wandering off to something new.
I planted a seed in a pot and watched it for a minute before my mind was already planning dinner, then work, then the holidays.
Carrying the full water pot back from the tap, I noticed that every time I thought of something else the water spilled, and I realised my mind was the same.
The pot of water spills at every step; so my mind, unsteady, loses the gift it was meant to carry.
Write a verse about the unsteady mind, which is like a pot of water carried over a rough road, spilling its calm at every jolt, and how only a slow, firm, mindful walk keeps it full.
pot of water, shaking mind
doha about the mind sloshing around like a pot of water carried on a bumpy road
wild mind, tame it
give me a doha on the jumpy mind pls
Even as I read my own exam paper, my thoughts were everywhere except the question, and I wrote nothing for an hour.
Write a doha about the restless mind that jumps from desire to desire, from worry to worry, never settling, and about the patient practice required to quiet and steady it.
Tied to a thousand strings of wishing, it leaps from craving to craving; who will teach this wanderer to sit?
jumpy mind, tame it
Write a verse about the jumping, chattering mind that cannot stay with the present for even a moment, always leaping to something new, and about the discipline that brings it back to peace.
doha on a distracted mind, mine to be exact
While my teacher spoke, I was thinking about lunch, my phone, an old quarrel, and what to wear on Friday, and none of it stayed.
Oh wanderer within, you chase a thousand wishes and catch none; come, sit with me for a moment.
doha about the mind that churns constantly like a churn
churning mind, restless
Last night I lay awake with my head turning like a churn, replaying the same conversation, and no peace came until I got up and stopped.
Compose a doha about the mind that churns endlessly, throwing up thoughts, worries, and memories, never settling long enough for the butter of peace to come, and needing to be slowed down.
Round and round the mind is churned, but only when it rests does the cream of quiet rise.
doha on the unruly mind, mirror and elephant if possible
The mind is a mirror shaken by a wandering breeze, an elephant maddened and loose; who has the goad to still it?
mirror, elephant, wandering mind
My mind is like an elephant that won't be led and a mirror in a shaking hand, and every time I try to pray it stampedes off.
Write a doha about the restless mind that is like a mirror in an unsteady hand, showing nothing clearly, and like an elephant running wild, until the goad of practice brings it to a calm halt.
Thought is carried here, there, everywhere, and nowhere at last, and the mind never sits for one breath.
I have twelve tabs open, three half-written letters, and a mind that wanders off before I finish a single sentence of anything.

Give me a verse about the person who cannot settle on any one task, who starts ten things and finishes none, whose attention runs after every new sound, and who needs to learn the patience of staying put.
short doha on being unable to focus
scattered thoughts, no focus
Write a verse about the river of the mind, always flowing, always chasing something new, unable to rest in any place, and how it needs the banks of discipline to become a calm and useful stream.
The mind rushes like a river after rain, carrying every stray thought along; who can build the bank that guides its flow?
doha on a river of thoughts that never stops?
river of thoughts
I walked beside the river trying to think of nothing, but my thoughts rushed ahead faster than the water, and none of them were worth anything.
In meditation class, I tried to count my breaths and got to three before my mind raced off to my to-do list.
doha for taming a wild mind
No force can tame the mind that wanders, no scolding calms it, only love and long practice.
Compose a verse about the untamed mind that rushes down every lane of desire, deaf to reason, and that can only be calmed by gentle, patient, and loving practice repeated for years.
untamed mind
doha on the river that is my wandering thoughts

Write a doha about the mind like a river that never stays in one bed, overflowing here, drying there, wandering from bank to bank, and only reaching peace when it learns to flow in one steady direction.
I stood by the river in the evening, watching it wander and braid, and thought, that is just how my mind behaves all day.
The river of the mind has no rest, wanders in a thousand bends; only the depth of stillness calls it back.
river, wandering thoughts
The swan glides in peace on a still pool, but my mind darts as though a hundred stones had been thrown in it.
Compose a verse about the restless mind that longs to be like a swan gliding on a calm lake, but is stirred again and again by every passing thought, and learns calm only through discipline.
The swan on the lake in our park glides without effort, and I envy it as my thoughts jump from topic to topic in my head.
doha on the mind that won't be calm like a swan
swan, wandering mind
The moon sits calm above the night, but the mind in its cage flutters, restless, wishing for the whole sky.
doha on a mind like a moon in a cage
moon, cage, restless mind
Write a verse about the mind that wanders even when the moon is gazing down, that beats against the cage of the body like a trapped bird, and that finds peace only when taught to sit still.
Lying awake under the moon I felt my mind beating inside my skull like a bird in a cage, wanting to be elsewhere.

Write a doha about the mind that runs after one desire after another, reaching for what it wants and instantly turning toward something new, and so never knowing the rest that comes from being content.
doha about the mind that keeps wanting the next thing
Every time I get something I wanted, my mind is already off looking for the next thing, and the satisfaction lasts about a minute.
Desire after desire, a ceaseless chain of wanting, and the mind runs behind each one, breathless, never arrived.
chasing, never arriving
Write a verse about the restless mind that keeps running through thorns of worry and desire, scratched and tired, but unable to stop until it is taught to sit down quietly and be still.
I keep chasing after new worries, every one a thorn in my side, and my mind just runs from one to the next with no rest at all.
a doha about my mind stepping on thorns of worry
thorn, wandering mind
The mind leaps from thorn to thorn, bleeding and not learning; who will teach the wanderer to rest?
At the crossroads a leaf is whirled by the wind, and so is my mind, every road calling, none walked.
Compose a doha about the mind, like a leaf blown at a crossroads, never choosing a path, turned this way and that by every breath of desire, and in need of a firm will to settle down.
At the crossroads of life, with all the choices before me, my mind blows around like a leaf and I can't settle on any path.
doha on a leaf at a crossroads, i mean my mind
crossroads, leaf, restless mind
short doha on training the mind to stay
Hold, O wanderer, the scattered strands of thinking; for the more you run, the farther you are from where you wished to be.
Every morning I try to sit for ten minutes, and every morning my thoughts pull me around the world before the timer rings.
Give me a verse about the ever-moving mind and the practice that gradually trains it to stay with one breath, one word, and one moment, until it is no longer pulled away by every sound.
calm the mind
restless, fidgety mind
why is my mind so restless? doha please

Compose a doha about the nature of the mind which never rests, which fills each empty moment with plans, fears, and memories, and which only grows quiet when it has been patiently trained over many years.
I got into bed exhausted but my mind kept replaying the day, planning the next, and arguing with people who were not even there.
Unsleeping, unresting, the mind runs through the night and the day; who will lead it back to quiet?
While I worked at the weaver's loom my thoughts rocked like a boat in a storm, and the shuttle kept missing its row.
doha on a mind like a rocking boat at a weaver's loom

Write a verse about the weaver's loom whose shuttle runs back and forth like the mind from thought to thought, and the little boat rocked by every wave, and how stillness is learned only by long practice.
The loom clatters, the boat rocks, and the mind rides every motion; who will teach it to be still?
loom, boat, unsteady mind
Write a verse about the mind carried on the palanquin of desire, shaken by every step of its bearers, never able to reach its true place, until it steps down and walks quietly on its own feet.
doha about the mind riding a palanquin of desires
On the long journey to the wedding I kept shifting in my seat, rocking like a palanquin, and my thoughts jumped around the whole way.
The palanquin sways, the passenger sways, and I, the wanderer, am carried far from where I meant to go.
palanquin, restless mind
The mind flutters like a moth around every glow, singed by each and returning to the next.
doha about a mind like a moth that keeps flying toward everything shiny
Write a verse about the mind like a moth that is drawn to every bright thing, circles, burns, forgets its pain, and goes again to the next glow, until it learns to rest in the dark.
I am like a moth with my phone, circling every notification, and my mind never rests on one thing for long.
moth, flitting mind
Like cotton drifting on a restless breeze, my thoughts float everywhere, and nothing is gathered but ash.
After my plans burned out and turned to ash, my thoughts drifted everywhere like loose cotton and I could not gather them.
Write a verse about the mind scattered like cotton fluff in the wind, impossible to gather, and the ash of burnt-out plans that it leaves behind, until it is taught to stay in one place.
doha about a mind scattered like cotton fluff and ash
cotton, ash, scattered mind
Even in the quiet of the night, my mind runs through lists, memories, regrets, and possibilities, and I only fall asleep when I am too tired to think.

Compose a verse about the mind that moves tirelessly through the day and still runs at night, without pause, without end, and about the stillness that comes when it finally stops trying to get somewhere.
O mind, tireless wanderer, hasten not after the hundred roads of wishing; the destination is here, within.
doha on a mind that can't rest even at night
never still, never resting
net, tangled thoughts
A net of a thousand knots is cast by the wandering mind, and it is caught in its own weaving.
doha about getting tangled up in my own thoughts like a net
Write a doha about the restless mind that keeps casting a net of plans and worries, tangling itself in its own endless thoughts, and about how to set it free by slowing down and watching.
I spent the whole evening tangled in my own thoughts, each one leading to three more, as if I were caught in a net I had woven myself.
I was at my own daughter's birthday party, but my head was in tomorrow's meeting, and I missed her big moment.
doha on how the mind jumps from past to future
Yesterday behind, tomorrow ahead, and the mind swings between them, never touching now.
Give me a verse about the mind which is never in the present, always regretting yesterday or fearing tomorrow, leaping between the two and missing the only moment it can ever really live in.
past, future, never now
unruly mind
I decided to give up scrolling for a day, but my thumb moved by itself and my mind jumped between a dozen things before an hour passed.
This mind that runs ahead without a guide; where will it stop, and who will hold it back?
doha for a mind I just can't control
Write a doha about the mind with no guide and no reins, running wherever it pleases, and about the loving discipline of a teacher that gently brings it to rest and gives it direction.
I keep jumping from one hobby to the next like someone swinging by a thread from tree to tree, never holding on to any one of them.
tree, thread, wandering mind
doha on the mind that swings from tree to tree on a thread of desire
Compose a verse about the mind hanging by the thread of desire and swinging from tree to tree, grabbing at every branch and holding none, and about learning to rest in one place.
From tree to tree on a trembling thread, the mind swings, always reaching for the next branch.
arrow, gold, restless mind
I chase promotions like an arrow after gold, and every time I get close, my attention swerves toward something bigger.
The arrow of the mind leaves the bow toward gold, then swerves to chase the next glitter.
doha about a mind that shoots off like an arrow after gold
Write a doha about the mind that shoots like an arrow in pursuit of gold, then turns in mid-flight toward another gleam, and never arrives at any target because it cannot stay on one.
a doha on mind chasing the sun all day
Compose a verse about the mind that rises with the sun and races across the day without rest, running from task to task, thought to thought, and finding no quiet until the evening finally falls.
From sunrise to sunset my mind never stops moving, it chases the heat of the day and never sits in the shade.
sun, restless mind
The mind follows the sun across the sky, restless from east to west, never resting at noon.
Like a flame that leaps from straw to straw, the mind devours one thought and rushes to another.
fire, restless mind
my mind is like a fire that jumps from one thing to the next, doha?
A thought about work lit another about money, and then another about family, and soon my whole head was ablaze like a spreading fire.
Write a doha about the mind that spreads like fire from one thought to another, consuming each and leaping to the next, and about the water of patient practice that brings it to a quiet end.
Write a verse about the mind whose thoughts float like tufts of cotton, carried wherever the breeze goes, never landing anywhere, and about the quiet practice that finally lets them settle.
cotton, floating thoughts
doha about thoughts floating like cotton that I can't catch
I tried to hold on to one idea but it drifted off like cotton in a breeze, and I ended up running after it around the room.
Light as cotton, the thoughts drift in every breeze, and none of them can be held in the palm.
The lotus rests on still water, the date palm bends with every gust; my mind sways even more, and finds no stillness.
Compose a doha about the lotus resting calmly on the pond and the date palm swaying in the wind, and the restless mind that cannot learn from either one how to be still and unshaken.
On the pond near our street, the lotus sits perfectly calm while the date palm shakes in the wind, and my mind is more like the palm.
doha: lotus is calm, date palm sways, my mind is neither
lotus, date palm, unsteady mind
short doha on stopping the thought spiral
A text message with no reply made my mind invent five reasons, ten fears, and one long imaginary argument by midnight.
stop overthinking

Write a verse about overthinking, the mind that takes one small worry and multiplies it a hundredfold, running in circles without ever reaching a conclusion, and the peace that comes from simply stopping.
One thought gives birth to ten, and the ten to a hundred, and the mind spins in its own making.
be still, mind
I finally told my thoughts to sit down and be quiet for once, and for about three seconds, they actually listened.
Write a doha to the mind itself, asking it to stop its restless wandering, to sit down quietly, to stop chasing every passing thing, and to discover that what it seeks is not far away.
Hear me, O mind: be still, be still! The peace you seek was never in the running.
doha addressed to my own busy mind
The oil press turns, the mind turns faster, and what remains of the grinding is only ash.
doha about restless mind, ash and an oil press
ash, oil press, grinding mind
I spent all day on the treadmill of my thoughts, ground down like an oil press, and by evening there was only grey ash left in me.
Write a doha about the mind that grinds through thoughts like an oil press that never stops, leaving only ash of tiredness behind, and about the rest it gets only when it is taught to pause.
Write a verse about the priest who recites the sacred verses perfectly but whose mind is running elsewhere, to money, to dinner, to the gossip of the day, and about the need to bring it back.
priest, wandering mind
doha on the priest whose thoughts wander during prayer
Our priest was chanting beautifully at the ceremony, but I could see his eyes drifting, and I realised that my own mind did the same when I prayed.
The priest chants with his lips while his mind goes off to count the day's coins; such is the wanderer.
Compose a verse about the mind that runs after fragrance like a musk deer, searching everywhere, while the forehead mark of devotion remains on the face and the heart elsewhere.
musk deer, forehead mark, wandering
doha on mind chasing a musk deer's scent and a forehead mark
I wear the forehead mark every day and still my mind runs searching like a musk deer for something it already has.
The musk deer searches the whole hillside for the scent it carries, and the mind wanders for the peace it wears.
parrot mind
Write a verse about the mind like a parrot that repeats the same thoughts over and over, fluttering from one phrase to another, never listening to its own words or finding a quiet moment.
doha on a parrot mind repeating thoughts
My parrot repeats the same three phrases all day long, and I realised my own mind is the same, going over the same complaints.
Like a parrot repeating itself, the mind chatters the same words without rest, never hearing what it says.
fish, flickering mind
short doha about a mind like a fish flopping around
The fish thrashes on dry ground; the mind thrashes in its thoughts; neither will rest until it is released.
Trying to sit still in meditation was like holding a fish in my hands, every thought slipping and twisting away from me.
Compose a doha about the mind that flips and darts like a fish out of water, never settling, never quiet, and about how it can only be calmed by returning to the stillness from which it came.
Write a verse about the gentle taming of a restless mind, not with force and punishment but with patience, kindness, and repeated returning, until it learns to come quietly when called.
taming the mind
My therapist told me not to fight my racing thoughts but to gently call them back each time they wander off.
Whoever would tame the mind must first befriend it with patience, for force only sends it running farther away.
how do i calm my mind? need a doha
lamp, flickering mind
When I study at night, the little lamp on my desk flickers and my thoughts flicker too, jumping between a hundred things.
The lamp flickers in the draught and the mind flickers with every thought; shield them both and they burn steady.
doha on a lamp that keeps flickering like my mind
Write a doha about the flame of attention, like a lamp in a draught, trembling at every breath of distraction, and about the patient shielding that lets it burn steady and bright.
The parrot flits to fragrant sandalwood and away again; so the mind, forever sampling, never stays.
doha about the parrot mind that loves sandalwood
Compose a verse about the mind that, like a parrot, flies from branch to branch chasing sweet scents, even sandalwood, never settling, until it learns to be content in one place.
In the sandalwood-scented hall I watched a parrot flit from one perch to another, and I thought of my own mind.
parrot, sandalwood, wandering mind
Write a doha about the mind that spills in every direction like salt shaken from a jar, and about the sacred forehead mark that cannot keep the thoughts of the wearer from wandering.
Salt scatters on the ground and a forehead mark is bright, but the mind that wears it wanders far away.
I put the forehead mark on every morning and then spill my attention everywhere, like salt in the kitchen.
doha on a mind that scatters like salt and a forehead mark
salt, forehead mark, restless
A heron stood perfectly still in the pond while my thoughts shot like arrows in all directions, and I felt a little ashamed.
doha on the heron's patience vs my restless mind and arrows of thought
heron, arrow, wild mind
Write a verse that sets the heron's patient stillness against the mind that shoots like an arrow at every ripple of distraction, and teaches how stillness, not speed, catches what is worth catching.
The heron stands patient and still, while the mind darts at every ripple like the arrow loosed from a hasty bow.
Call back your scattered thoughts at dusk, let them sit at your feet, and be at peace.
Give me a verse about how the mind runs outward in all ten directions and how, with practice, it can be gathered, brought back, and settled in one point of quiet attention.
i need a doha on keeping the mind in one place
Whenever my mind runs off in many directions, I try to call it back gently, and it comes slowly, one thought at a time.
gather the mind
doha about a ringing bell and a mirror, restless mind version
Every time the bell rings I lose my train of thought, and when I try to see myself clearly in the mirror of the mind, nothing holds still.
The bell rings, the mirror trembles, and the face within it is shattered into a thousand wanderings.
Write a doha about the mind like a mirror that shakes whenever a bell rings, never able to reflect clearly, and how only the silence after the bell lets the mirror be still and true.
bell, mirror, shaky mind
Write a verse about the sun moving steadily across the sky and the boat drifting on its calm course, while the restless mind alone refuses to settle and keeps racing in every direction.
sun, boat, wandering mind
On the boat at sunrise, everything was calm, but my mind raced about like a child that cannot sit.
doha on the sun, a boat, and my mind that never stops
The sun walks the sky without hurry, the boat drifts without will, yet the mind runs past them both.
A talker without a voice, a wanderer without feet, the mind goes everywhere and arrives nowhere.
chattering mind
I try to enjoy the silence of a walk but my brain keeps narrating, judging, and planning, as if it were afraid of the quiet.
Write a doha about the endless chatter of the mind, the unending monologue that comments on everything, worries about everything, and never lets us rest in the quiet that is so close.
why does my mind never stop talking
Watching the moon rise over the ocean, I felt my moods surge and retreat just like the waves, and I wished my mind could be as tidy.
The moon draws the ocean and the ocean heaves; so my mind rises and sinks with every passing pull.
doha on moon and ocean and a restless mind
moon, ocean, tidal mind
Compose a verse on the mind like the ocean rising and falling at the pull of the moon, restless, tidal, never settled, and on the calm that arrives only when it learns not to follow every pull.
doha about weaving and prayer beads with a mind that wanders
My mother counts her prayer beads and then suddenly stops mid-prayer because her mind went to her loom and the cloth she has not finished.
loom, prayer beads, wandering
The loom's shuttle flies, the prayer beads slip, but the mind walks off on its own long road.
Write a verse about the weaver at the loom and the devotee with prayer beads, both working with the hands while their minds go wandering, far away from the work and from the prayer.
